title: Authority of Scripture
definition: The authority of Scripture means that the written Word of God carries God's own authority and stands over the church, the believer, human opinion, tradition, and every claim of truth.
summary: Because Scripture is God's Word, it must be believed, obeyed, taught, and trusted above every competing voice.
christFocus: Jesus submitted to Scripture, fulfilled Scripture, quoted Scripture, and rebuked error by Scripture. His own life confirms the authority of God's written Word.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content: Authority of Scripture teaches that God's people must receive this truth under the authority of the Lord, allowing Scripture itself to define the doctrine rather than personal opinion, tradition, or culture.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content: This doctrine matters because it protects the believer from confusion and helps the church remain anchored in what God has actually spoken. Without this truth, faith can drift toward feelings, assumptions, or human wisdom.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: A disciple should respond to authority of scripture by reading the Word prayerfully, testing beliefs by Scripture, obeying what God reveals, and helping others handle the Bible with humility, clarity, and faith.

studySections.heading: Guardrails and Common Errors
studySections.content: This doctrine should not be used to win arguments while neglecting love, nor should it be separated from prayer, obedience, and dependence on the Holy Spirit. The goal is faithful submission to God, not mere possession of information.

sources: Scripture references listed in this doctrine entry.
